Divergence-based classifier for SAR/PolSAR features (R6)

Source: R/classifier.R
DivergenceClassifier.Rd

Implements the family of divergence-based classifiers of Ferreira, Coelho and Nascimento (2021). Each pixel is represented by the model fitted to the observations of a moving window (see sar_features()) and each class by the model fitted to its training pixels. A pixel is assigned to the class that minimises the chosen divergence between the two fitted models: $$\hat\imath = \arg\min_{i \in \{1, \ldots, g\}} d(\hat\theta_h, \hat\theta_i).$$

Two families of features are available:

"gaussian"

multivariate normal laws for the intensity vector, using the columns mean_* and cov_* of sar_features(). The class covariance combines the average local covariance and the covariance of the local means (law of total variance).

"wishart"

scaled complex Wishart laws for the full PolSAR covariance matrix, using the columns c11, c12_re, c12_im, ... of sar_features(). Since all laws share the number of looks, it only rescales the divergences and does not affect the classification.

The classifier is also available as the 'parsnip' model divergence_classifier(), for use in 'tidymodels' workflows.

References

Ferreira, J. A., Coelho, H. and Nascimento, A. D. C. (2021). A family of divergence-based classifiers for polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) imagery vector and matrix features. International Journal of Remote Sensing, 42(4), 1201–1229. doi:10.1080/01431161.2020.1826060

Public fields

family

"gaussian" or "wishart".

divergence

Divergence used (see divergence_gaussian()).

order

Order of the Rényi divergence.

kind

Form (1-4) of the Rényi divergence.

classes

Class labels.

prototypes

List with the fitted model of each class.

channels

Channels (Gaussian) or matrix order (Wishart) used.

DivergenceClassifier$new()

Create a classifier.

Usage

DivergenceClassifier$new(
  family = c("gaussian", "wishart"),
  divergence = c("renyi", "kl", "jeffreys", "bhattacharyya"),
  order = 0.5,
  kind = 1
)

Arguments

family

"gaussian" or "wishart".

divergence

"kl", "jeffreys", "bhattacharyya" or "renyi".

order

Order of the Rényi divergence, in (0, 1).

kind

Form of the Rényi divergence (1 to 4).

DivergenceClassifier$fit()

Fit the class prototypes.

Usage

DivergenceClassifier$fit(x, y)

Arguments

x

Data frame of features (see sar_features()); other columns are ignored.

y

Factor (or vector) of class labels.

DivergenceClassifier$distances()

Divergence between every row of x and every class.

Usage

DivergenceClassifier$distances(x)

Arguments

x

Data frame of features.

DivergenceClassifier$predict()

Predict classes, pseudo-probabilities or distances.

Usage

DivergenceClassifier$predict(x, type = c("class", "prob", "distance"))

Arguments

x

Data frame of features.

type

"class", "prob" (softmax of minus the divergences) or "distance".

Ignored.

Examples

img <- SARImage$new(SanFrancisco150)$crop(1:80, 1:80)
feats <- sar_features(img, window = 5)
feats$class <- factor(as.vector(SanFrancisco150_gt[1:80, 1:80]),
                      labels = c("ocean", "forest", "urban"))
set.seed(1)
train <- feats[sample(nrow(feats), 300), ]

clf <- DivergenceClassifier$new(family = "wishart", divergence = "renyi",
                                order = 0.5, kind = 3)
clf$fit(train, train$class)
pred <- clf$predict(feats)
mean(pred == feats$class)
#> [1] 0.9920313
head(clf$predict(feats, type = "distance"))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 3
#>   ocean forest urban
#>   <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1  1.72   6.56  9.48
#> 2  1.68   6.55  9.50
#> 3  1.65   6.53  9.50
#> 4  1.69   6.59  9.58
#> 5  1.71   6.66  9.68
#> 6  1.62   6.51  9.51
